en: He whose form is light that never sets, who is one within both lights and darkness, and within whom both lights and darkness abide.
That very Supreme Lord is the inherent nature of all beings; for the entire collection of existing things is His power, consisting of His lordship.
And power does not seek separation from the nature of the possessor of power;
there is an eternal identity between these two, just as between fire and its capacity to burn. (3)
That very god Bhairava, whose characteristic is the sustaining of the universe,
indeed reflects everything within his own self through his power for the sake of one who perceives him.
This supreme Goddess belongs to Him alone, ever eager for the self-reflection of His own nature;
she whose fullness in all existences is neither deficient nor excessive. (5)
This Lord, ever eager for the flavor of play with this Goddess,
the omnipresent one, simultaneously effects various creations and dissolutions.
That this [consciousness] performs what is exceedingly difficult to accomplish is its unsurpassed nature;
this alone is its autonomy, its sovereignty, and its nature as pure awareness. (7)
Limited luminosity is indeed the defining characteristic of the insentient;
for consciousness, being distinct from the insentient, is not so measured.
Thus, for this autonomous [Lord] who differentiates through his own innate power, the emanations and withdrawals residing within his own self exist as his very nature. (9)
Among them, there is an extreme variety consisting of what is above, below, and horizontal;
these are the worlds and their constituent parts, as well as whatever perceptions of pleasure and pain exist.
The non-recognition of this [reality] is indeed described as its independence;
that very thing is truly saṃsāra for the deluded, which is a source of terror. (11)

Whether it has come from the grace of that [Lord], or from the oral tradition of the Guru, or from the scripture of the Supreme Lord— whichever source it may have come from— it is through the very essence of His favor.
That thorough knowledge of reality is liberation according to the Supreme Lord;
that is the fullness of the awakened, and it is remembered as liberation while living (jīvanmukti). // 13 //
Both this bondage and liberation do not differ from the essential nature of the Supreme Lord; for in reality, there is no duality within the Supreme Lord.
Thus, Bhairava—the inherent nature of all existents—is contemplated as resting upon the lotus of the trident consisting of the powers of will, action, and knowledge. 15.
In order to awaken disciples of delicate intellect directly,
these fifteen verses have been uttered by Abhinavagupta.
Gandharvanagara (The City of the Gandharvas)
